events.title: Elixir 0.1.0 released
events.summary: José Valim released Elixir v0.1.0 on March 2, 2011 — a Ruby-inspired language on the Erlang BEAM VM.
events.about: Elixir runs on Erlang's OTP with metaprogramming, pipelines (`|>`), and Phoenix for web. Powers Discord's real-time infrastructure, Pinterest backends, and IoT systems needing millions of connections. You get Erlang's fault tolerance with syntax closer to Ruby and modern tooling.

narrative.whyChosen: Elixir made the BEAM VM accessible to developers who found Erlang syntax daunting.
narrative.whyImportant: It revived interest in actor-model concurrency for web and real-time systems in the 2010s.
narrative.problemSolved: Erlang was proven for telecom but had a steep syntax curve; Valim wanted Ruby-like ergonomics on BEAM.

events.title: Internet Explorer 9 released
events.summary: Microsoft released Internet Explorer 9 on March 14, 2011 with hardware-accelerated graphics, a cleaner UI, and improved HTML5 and CSS3 support.
events.about: IE 9 was Microsoft's answer to Chrome: a GPU-accelerated rendering pipeline, pinned sites, and a focus on web standards. It was the last IE version many enterprises standardized on before Windows 10 and Edge.

narrative.whyChosen: IE 9 was Microsoft's most standards-focused Internet Explorer release.
narrative.whyImportant: Hardware acceleration and HTML5 support narrowed the gap with modern browsers.
narrative.problemSolved: IE 8 could not keep pace with Chrome's speed and developer mindshare.

events.title: Firefox 4 released
events.summary: Mozilla released Firefox 4 on March 22, 2011 with a new UI, hardware acceleration, and faster JavaScript — downloaded over 7 million times on launch day.
events.about: Firefox 4 was Mozilla's big refresh: Panorama tab groups, sync, WebGL, and a Chrome-like single-field URL bar. The record launch day showed Firefox still had mass appeal before Chrome became dominant.

narrative.whyChosen: Firefox 4 was Mozilla's flagship response to Chrome's rapid rise.
narrative.whyImportant: Hardware acceleration and WebGL kept Firefox in the graphics-heavy web race.
narrative.problemSolved: Firefox 3.6 felt slow and dated against Chrome's fast release cadence.
